small_guidance:
- Add larger autotune tiles (BLOCK_OC=128/BLOCK_OW=256, num_warps=8, num_stages=3-4) and try BLOCK_OC=256/BLOCK_OW=64 — the GEMM-K is only IC*KW=96 per inner tl.dot so larger M/N tiles amortize the bias/activation epilogue and improve tensor-core utilization.
- Fuse the KW loop into the K dimension of a single tl.dot per (kd, kh): load x as [BLOCK_OW, KW*IC] and w as [BLOCK_OC, KW*IC] once per kh, reducing the number of dot calls from KD*KH*KW=27 to KD*KH=9 and giving a fatter K (=96) for better tensor-core throughput.
- Mask OW tail with `other=0.0` only when pid_ow is the last tile (split kernel via specialization on `OW % BLOCK_OW == 0`), and align BLOCK_OW so OW=62 isn't padded heavily — current BLOCK_OW=64 wastes 2 lanes per row.
large_guidance:
- Switch to an implicit-GEMM with the K dimension being `IC*KD*KH*KW` (=864) and tile it (BLOCK_K=32 or 64), so one program does a single accumulating matmul over all kernel taps rather than 27 separate tl.dots. This lets Triton's pipeliner overlap loads with mma and exposes the full reduction to tensor cores.
- Tile spatial as (OD*OH*OW) flattened with BLOCK_M on the spatial axis and BLOCK_N on OC; precompute per-K-index offset tables (delta_d, delta_h, delta_w, delta_ic) on host and pass as int32 tensors so index math inside the kernel is a single add+gather.
- Keep output in NHWC (or NDHWC) layout end-to-end and write directly in that layout, dropping the final permute-to-NCDHW (which currently happens implicitly via the strided output store pattern); if a downstream op needs NCDHW, do one fused transpose-store rather than scattered strided writes.
